title: The Secret in the Office
excerpt: Erotic office romance · Forbidden attraction · Workplace drama
content:
By Monday morning, Victoria had made a decision.

She would not risk Daniel's career, her own reputation, or the trust that made their relationship possible. She had contacted HR about transferring his supervision to another manager, and she intended to keep their private lives separate from their professional responsibilities.

Daniel arrived at nine precisely.

"Morning, Ms. Hayes."

The formal greeting made her smile.

"Morning, Mr. Cole. Your revised assignment is on your desk."

He glanced at the folder. "Already replacing me?"

"Temporarily. Your new supervisor starts overseeing your work today."

His expression changed. "You actually did it."

"I told you I would."

He studied her for a moment. "You know what this means, right?"

"What?"

He leaned closer, lowering his voice.

"Now you can't use work as an excuse to avoid having dinner with me."

Victoria tried to look stern.

"You're very confident for someone who has only just received his first proper internship assignment."

"I'm confident because I asked you a question, and you haven't answered it."

She looked at him, fighting a smile.

"Friday. Seven o'clock."

His face lit up. "Is that a yes?"

"It's a dinner invitation, Daniel. Don't make me regret it."

"I wouldn't dare."

For the rest of the day, they behaved impeccably. No lingering touches, no suggestive remarks, no private conversations behind closed doors. Their colleagues noticed nothing unusual.

But Victoria found herself checking the clock far more often than she should.

On Friday evening, she arrived at the restaurant in a black dress, her hair falling loosely around her shoulders. Daniel was already waiting.

He stood when he saw her.

"Wow."

"That's your entire vocabulary?"

"I'm trying to be respectful."

"How's that going?"

"Terribly."

She laughed, and the last of her nervousness disappeared.

Dinner was easier than she expected. They talked about his ambitions, her career, the mistakes they had made, and the things they wanted from life outside the office.

Daniel admitted he had been nervous about pursuing her.

"I didn't want you to think I was using the internship to get close to you," he said.

"And I didn't want you to think your future depended on whether I liked you."

"That's why I agreed to the transfer."

Victoria reached across the table and took his hand.

"That was the right decision."

He squeezed her fingers. "So what happens now?"

She tilted her head.

"Now, we see whether we like each other when there are no spreadsheets, deadlines, or office doors between us."

"And if we do?"

She smiled.

"Then you can ask me on a second date."

"Only a second?"

"Don't get greedy."

He laughed, and she realized how much she liked the sound.

Outside, the night air was cool. They walked slowly toward her car, neither in a hurry to say goodbye.

Daniel stopped beside her.

"Can I kiss you?"

Victoria looked at him for a moment before answering.

"Yes."

The kiss was warmer and more certain than the first. There was no deadline waiting, no office phone about to ring, no reason to pretend their feelings were merely an inconvenient distraction.

When they separated, Daniel rested his forehead against hers.

"I think I'm in trouble," he whispered.

Victoria smiled.

"You're not my intern anymore, Daniel."

"Then what am I?"

She kissed him once more.

"That's what we're going to find out."

And for the first time in a long while, Victoria was perfectly happy not to know what came next.
